issues.description: Problem statement requires the Farm to initialize its ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments (a public no-arg constructor). The solution's Farm class only defines a constructor Farm(int initialCapacity) and does not provide a no-arg constructor, while the template/problem examples show usage new Farm(). This constructor-parameter mismatch will confuse students and can break expected usage or tests that instantiate Farm with no arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a public no-argument constructor public Farm() that initializes animals = new ArrayList<>(); (optionally keep the existing Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor). Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to explicitly require a Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor and adjust example usages accordingly. The preferred fix is to provide the no-arg constructor so examples and tests using new Farm() compile and behave as described.
